findings.evidence: Parser adds `CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` grammar (`pkg/parser/parser.y:16183`) and the AST type is a `ast.DDLNode` (`pkg/parser/ast/ddl.go:39`). PlanBuilder routes any `ast.DDLNode` to `buildDDL` (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:582`), and `buildDDL` unconditionally returns `&DDL{Statement: node}` even when the type-switch has no matching case (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5696`). `DDLExec.Next` has no case (and no `default:`) for `*ast.CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` (`pkg/executor/ddl.go:160`), so `err` remains nil and the executor returns success (`pkg/executor/ddl.go:248`). `ShowExec.fetchAll` likewise has no case for `ast.ShowMaskingPolicies` and falls through to `return nil` (`pkg/executor/show.go:181`, `pkg/executor/show.go:299`).
findings.fix: Until masking policy is fully implemented end-to-end, explicitly reject these statements (return a clear unsupported error) instead of silently succeeding. Minimal safety net: add a `default:` branch in `pkg/executor/ddl.go` to error on unknown `ast.DDLNode` types, and add either a `case ast.ShowMaskingPolicies:` implementation or a default error path in `pkg/executor/show.go` for unknown `ShowStmtType`. Also add corresponding privilege/visitInfo handling in `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` for `*ast.CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` and `ast.ShowMaskingPolicies` once supported.
findings.impact: User-visible SQL (`CREATE MASKING POLICY`, `SHOW MASKING POLICIES`) can report success while having no effect (DDL) or returning empty results (SHOW). For a data-masking feature, this can create a false sense of protection and lead to sensitive data exposure. The planner also does not attach explicit privilege requirements for these new statements, which becomes a security issue once execution is added.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): `CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` occurrences are still confined to parser/AST (no executor/planner handling found), and `pkg/executor/ddl.go` / `pkg/executor/show.go` still lack handling/default error for these new statement types.
findings.verify: 1) Execute `CREATE MASKING POLICY p ON t(c) AS c` and ensure it either creates the policy (and is observable) or returns a clear unsupported error; it must not silently succeed. 2) Execute `SHOW MASKING POLICIES FOR t` and ensure it returns an error or correct rows (not empty-by-default). 3) Verify privilege enforcement denies unprivileged users once supported.
findings.what: New masking policy statements become parseable, but are not handled by planner/executor, so they can silently succeed without applying any masking (DDL) or return empty results (SHOW).

subject: parser,ast: support column masking grammar (#66031)
summary: This commit adds MASKING/POLICIES keywords plus AST+grammar for `CREATE MASKING POLICY`, masking-policy ALTER TABLE specs, and `SHOW MASKING POLICIES`. A critical integration gap remains: the newly parseable statement types are not handled by planner/executor paths and can return success with no effect (DDL) or empty results (SHOW), which is especially risky for a security/privacy feature.
